chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
"When the slave owns one-sixth of his value, he is asked for more (to complete the full value) and it is accepted."

key_terms.أُسْتُسْعِيَ: He is asked for more (to complete the amount)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave owns one-sixth of their value for emancipation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istis'a'* (compulsion) in manumission, where the master is legally compelled to accept the remaining payment once the slave presents one-sixth of the agreed value. This ruling, rooted in Shia jurisprudence, ensures that the slave's partial fulfillment of the contract triggers the master's obligation to complete the emancipation process, reflecting the ethical imperative of freeing slaves in Islam.
